safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(the hamza) is for confirmatory interrogation [Note: or for expressing wonder.], (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative, a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, i.e. "He did a mighty deed" [Note: or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl whose governing element is a verb.], (بأصحاب) is attached to (فعل)..
Clause: «لم تر ... » has no grammatical position; it is inceptive.
And the clause: «فعل ربّك ... » is in the position of accusative, standing in for the two objects of تر, which is suspended by the interrogative كيف.

* Morphology:
(الفيل): the name of the well-known animal; its wazn is فعل with kasra then sukūn.

* Benefits:
- The Companions of the Elephant:
Historians and biographers mention that Abraha ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ, king of Yemen, built a church in Ṣanʿāʾ and called it al-Qullays, and wished to divert the pilgrims to it. A man from Kināna went out and sat in it at night and defiled it, which angered him. It was also said: a party of Arabs lit a fire, the wind carried it and it burned the church. So he swore to demolish the Kaʿba. He set out with the Abyssinians, and with him an elephant named Maḥmūd, which was strong and huge, and twelve other elephants. When the army came, ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib went out to him and offered him a third of the wealth of Tihāma if he would turn back, but he refused and headed to demolish the Kaʿba. Whenever they directed the elephant toward the Sanctuary it knelt and would not budge, and if they directed it toward Yemen or Syria it trotted. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent birds, each bird carrying a stone in its beak and two stones in its feet, smaller than a chickpea. The stone would fall on a man's head and come out of his rear; so they fled and perished. Abraha died, his chest splitting open from his heart. His vizier escaped, with a bird hovering over him, until he reached the Negus and told him the story; when he finished it, the stone fell on him and he dropped dead before him.
Most of the scholars of biography and history and the people of exegesis hold that the event of the Elephant took place in the year in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was born, so as to be a prominent landmark in history and an enduring honour for the Prophet ﷺ.

safi-cedvel:2-5.t:
* I'rab:
(the hamza) is like the first. (في تضليل) is attached to an omitted element, a second direct object. (عليهم) is attached to (أرسل), (أبابيل) is a naʿt of (طيرا), accusative, and it is denied tanwīn because of the form of the "ultimate plural" (muntahā al-jumūʿ). (بحجارة) is attached to (ترميهم), (من سجّيل) is attached to an adjective of (حجارة), (كعصف) is attached to an omitted element, a second direct object..
Clause: «لم يجعل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «أرسل ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يجعل.
And the clause: «ترميهم ... » is in the position of accusative, a second naʿt of (طيرا).
And the clause: «جعلهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أرسل.

* Morphology:
(2) تضليل: the regular maṣdar of the quadriliteral ضلّل; its wazn is تفعيل.
(3) أبابيل: a collective noun (ism jamʿ) with no singular from its own wording; it was said that its singular is إبّول on the wazn of سنّور, or أبّول on the wazn of عصفور, or إبّيل on the wazn of سكّين, or إبّال on the wazn of مفتاح.
(5) عصف: a name for the leaves of crops or their chaff, on the wazn of the maṣdar فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(5) مأكول: a passive participle from the triliteral أكل; its wazn is مفعول.

* Rhetoric:
Simile: in His saying, the Exalted: «فَجَعَلَهُمْ كَعَصْفٍ مَأْكُولٍ».
Here He likened them to eaten chaff – which is the straw of wheat – for its being emptied of its grain and blown about; or He likened the severing of their limbs to the scattering of the parts of dung that animals have eaten and excreted. It is thus a likening of a sensory thing to a sensory thing.
